## Background

![look how many ions are prob in this water](https://media.newyorker.com/photos/6331dc33105812508a066849/master/w_2560%2Cc_limit/PR%2520Hurricane%2520Final.jpg)

In September 1989, Hurricane Hugo hit Puerto Rico. This project analyzes water quality data from various freshwater systems in Puerto Rico after the hurricane. The goal is to recreate figure 3 from Schaefer et al. (2000).

![Schaefer et al. (2000)](https://eds-214-reproducibility-m26.github.io/course-materials/interactive/images/Schaefer_etal_2020_fig3.png)

## Data

Data was acesssed via McDowell and International Institute Of Tropical Forestry (IITF) (2024). Data was cleaned in the 1_clean_data.R file.

Load libraries and data
```{r}
#| output: false
library(tidyverse)
cdat <- read_csv('../output/cleaned_data.csv')
```

## Methods

To prepare data for plotting, 9-week moving averages were calculated for each site and ion. Data was also filtered to relevant years. Functions for this are located in the R folder, and the data cleaning is contained in 1_clean_data.R. 

We applied `pivot_longer()` to the cleaned data in order to get an Ion and Concentration column. This allows us to facet wrap on Ion.

```{r}
cdat_long <- cdat |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(k_mgl, no3, mg_mgl, ca, nh4),
    names_to = 'Ion',
    values_to = 'Concentration'
  )
```

## Results

```{r}
#| warning: false
plot1 <- cdat_long |>
  ggplot(
    aes(x = window_start, y = Concentration, linetype = site)
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(Ion),
    scales = 'free',
    ncol = 1,
    strip.position = "left",
    labeller = labeller(
      Ion = c(
        'ca' = 'Ca mg l-1',
        'k_mgl' = 'K mg l-1',
        'mg_mgl' = 'Mg mg l-1',
        'nh4' = 'NH4-N µg l-1',
        'no3' = 'NO3-N µg l-1'
      )
    )
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ymd('1989-09-17'), linetype = 'dashed') +
  labs(x = 'Years', y = 'Concentration of Ions') +
  theme_bw()

plot1
```

Concentrations of potassium, calcium, magnesium and ammonia have increased since the hurricane hit. They have gradually decreased in the 4 years since the hurricane, except for magnesium which has increased.
